\[
T(x, y) = \operatorname{mean}_{s \times s}(I) - C,
\quad
I_{\text{out}} = \begin{cases} 255 & I > T \\ 0 & \text{otherwise} \end{cases},
\qquad s = 15,\ C = 5
\]

The formula shows the default parameter values.

where

- \(T(x, y)\): The local threshold
- \(s\): The window size
- \(C\): The offset

The threshold at each pixel is the mean of the s by s window around the pixel, minus the offset C. This follows scikit-image's threshold_local. So a pixel turns white when it is brighter than its surroundings by more than C. Slow changes of lighting move the mean and the pixel together, so they do not change the result. The result is 255 where the value is above the threshold and 0 elsewhere, or the reverse with Invert. OpenCV's adaptiveThreshold is similar, but rounds the mean to whole levels and sizes its Gaussian differently.
